Pop the caller's frame only after allocating argument work and reloading.\n; The callee publishes its incoming argument before any allocation/safepoint.\ndefine i64 @contract_tail(i64 %incoming, i64 %remaining) noinline sanitize_address {\nentry:\n  %slot = alloca i64, align 8\n  %root = alloca %Root, align 8\n  store i64 %incoming, ptr %slot, align 8\n  call void @root_push(ptr %root, ptr %slot)\n  %done = icmp eq i64 %remaining, 0\n  br i1 %done, label %finish, label %again\nfinish:\n  call void @minor_collect()\n  %final = load i64, ptr %slot, align 8\n  call void @root_pop(ptr %root)\n  ret i64 %final\nagain:\n  %garbage = call i64 @allocate(i64 1, i64 0)\n  %gp = inttoptr i64 %garbage to ptr\n  store i64 1, ptr %gp, align 8\n  call void @minor_collect()\n  %live = load i64, ptr %slot, align 8\n  %next = sub i64 %remaining, 1\n  call void @root_pop(ptr %root)\n  %result = musttail call i64 @contract_tail(i64 %live, i64 %next)\n  ret i64 %result\n}\n",
    "5ca4ce0a019cabf73ae24ce576223ff13c7536a9ae98f472c5c8371ce45b7667": "/* Medaka native runtime \u2014 Stage 2.4 DE-RISKING SPIKE (slices 1\u20133).\n *\n * This is NOT the real runtime.  It is the minimal C stub the spike's emitted\n * LLVM IR links against to prove the emit -> clang -> link -> run -> diff\n * toolchain end-to-end (see compiler/STAGE2-DESIGN.md \u00a72.4 and the \"Value\n * representation & calling convention\" section of compiler/RUNTIME-DESIGN.md).\n *\n * Scope discipline (matches the emitter): integers, floats, booleans, let, if,\n * functions, (slice 3) algebraic data types + pattern matching, and (native\n * extern catalog slice 1) heap Strings + the minimal string/IO leaf externs\n * (`mdk_str_lit`, `mdk_print_str`, `mdk_int_to_string`).  ADT and String cells\n * box through the same mdk_alloc below.  No closures / records / dispatch beyond\n * what the emitter already drives.\n *\n * VALUE REPRESENTATION (PROVISIONAL \u2014 see RUNTIME-DESIGN.md, revisable):\n *   A Medaka value is a uniform 64-bit word (`i64` in the IR).\n *     - Integers are IMMEDIATE: word = (n << 1) | 1   (low bit 1 => tagged int).\n *       63-bit signed range; untag = word >> 1 (arithmetic).\n *     - Booleans reuse the immediate-int encoding (0 / 1) \u2014 slice 1 is statically\n *       typed, so the emitter picks the print routine by static type and never\n *       needs to tell a Bool from an Int at runtime.  A polymorphic rep will need\n *       to (a documented limitation surfaced by this spike).\n *     - Floats are BOXED: word is a pointer (low bit 0, malloc is >=8-aligned) to\n *       a 16-byte heap cell { i64 header = TAG_FLOAT, double payload }.  This is\n *       what surfaces \"floats don't fit in a tagged-int word\" -> the alloc below.\n *     - ADT values are BOXED (slice 3): word is a pointer to a cell\n *       { i64 tag (constructor name hashed), field0, field1, ... } \u2014 one 8-byte\n *       word each.  Same boxed-pointer discipline as Float, extended to n fields;\n *       allocated through the same mdk_alloc.\n *\n * The tag arithmetic lives in the EMITTED IR (so the cost is visible); these\n * helpers take/return *native* C scalars (the emitter untags/unboxes first).\n *\n * GC: the spike now runs on the Boehm conservative collector (bdw-gc).  mdk_alloc\n *   routes to GC_malloc; immediates are odd words (low bit 1), so Boehm never\n *   mistakes an Int/Char/Bool/Unit/nullary-ctor for a pointer, and every boxed\n *   value is an 8-byte-aligned real pointer Boehm tracks natively\n *   (RUNTIME-DESIGN.md \u00a78.0 fact 3, \u00a78.1).  Precise GC remains future work.\n */\n/* _GNU_SOURCE: on glibc/Linux, pthread_getattr_np (used by the P0-2 fault\n * backstop to find the worker stack bounds) is only declared under it.  No-op on\n * Darwin, which uses pthread_get_stackaddr_np instead. */\n#ifndef _GNU_SOURCE\n#define _GNU_SOURCE\n#endif\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <errno.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <limits.h>\n#include <math.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <stdnoreturn.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <sys/time.h>\n#include <time.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <signal.h>\n#include <sys/socket.h>\n#include <netinet/in.h>\n#include <netinet/tcp.h>\n#include <netdb.h>\n#include <arpa/inet.h>\n#include <poll.h>\n#include <fcntl.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <sys/random.h>\n#ifdef __APPLE__\n#include <mach-o/dyld.h>\n#endif\n#include <pthread.h>\n/* GC_THREADS MUST be defined before <gc.h> so Boehm exposes GC_pthread_create /\n * GC_pthread_join.  The compiler runs its whole pipeline on a large-stack worker\n * thread (see `int main` at the bottom of this file); a thread created with raw\n * pthread_create would NOT have its stack registered as a GC root, so Boehm would\n * collect still-live objects and corrupt the heap.  GC_pthread_create registers\n * the worker's stack, keeping conservative scanning correct on it. */\n#define GC_THREADS\n#include <gc.h>\n/* gc_inline.h asserts each allocation's size with GC_size, a call per cell, unless\n * GC_ASSERT is already defined.  mdk_alloc's fast path must not pay it. */\n#define GC_ASSERT(expr) ((void)0)\n#include <gc/gc_inline.h>\n\n/* Initial heap to pre-expand, in bytes, for the COMPILER/CLI only: the stage-B\n * provenance object (test/build_native_medaka.sh) defines this for ./medaka. Every\n * other link (user programs, the emitter, the seed) keeps the weak 0, so none of\n * them pre-expand the heap. An explicit GC_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE in the environment wins. */\n__attribute__((weak)) const long long mdk_gc_initial_heap_bytes = 0;\n\n/* Initialize Boehm once before main().  This runtime owns `int main` (bottom of\n * this file); the emitted IR's entry is `mdk_program_main`, which we run on a\n * GC_pthread_create'd large-stack worker thread.  A constructor runs first, near\n * the bottom of the process stack, which is where GC_INIT wants to capture the\n * (main-thread) stack base; the worker thread's own stack is registered\n * separately by GC_pthread_create.  GC_malloc would otherwise lazily init on its\n * first call. */\n\n__attribute__((constructor)) static void mdk_gc_init(void) {\n  GC_INIT();\n  if (mdk_gc_initial_heap_bytes > 0 && !getenv(\"GC_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE\"))\n    GC_expand_hp((size_t)mdk_gc_initial_heap_bytes);\n  /* Perf tuning (compiler/PERF-RESULTS.md): Medaka workloads are\n   * allocation-heavy and mostly short-lived (the emitter alone allocates\n   * ~4200 cells/run plus every cons/closure/ADT).  The default free-space\n   * divisor (3) collects aggressively to keep RSS low; we trade some memory\n   * for fewer collection pauses by letting the heap grow further between GCs.\n   * Env var GC_FREE_SPACE_DIVISOR still overrides this if set. */\n  if (!getenv(\"GC_FREE_SPACE_DIVISOR\")) GC_set_free_space_divisor(1);\n}\n\n/* Allocate `n` bytes in the GC heap, with GC_malloc's semantics (conservative,\n * collected); every extern that RETURNS a Medaka value goes through this single\n * entry point, so the malloc->GC swap was one function (RUNTIME-DESIGN.md \u00a72a).\n * The result is >=8-byte-aligned, zeroed memory \u2014 satisfying the boxed-pointer\n * alignment contract the value rep relies on.  The emitted IR declares this with\n * allockind(\"alloc,zeroed\") and noalias, so LLVM may delete an unused cell and\n * forward its stores: the function must stay free of observable side effects\n * beyond the allocation, and must return zeroed memory.\n *\n * On libgc 8.2, small cells come from this thread's own free lists through\n * Boehm's inline allocator (gc_inline.h) rather than GC_malloc, which per call\n * saves its registers, looks up libgc's thread-local lists and goes through\n * GC_malloc_kind (#503).  The contract holds the same way GC_malloc's own\n * thread-local path keeps it, which uses the same macro:\n *   - size: a request takes the granule count GC_malloc would give it, `n` plus\n *     the one byte Boehm appends when interior pointers are recognised, rounded\n *     up to 16-byte granules.  gc_inline.h leaves that byte to the caller, and the\n *     collector does not trace an object's last word on the assumption it is\n *     there.  Any `n` that is not below MDK_ALLOC_INLINE_LIMIT as an unsigned\n *     size, a negative one included, goes to GC_malloc unchanged.\n *   - zeroed: a NORMAL-kind free list holds cleared objects whose first word\n *     links to the next; the hit path clears that word.\n *   - retention: the list heads live in an uncollectable block, which the\n *     collector scans, so each list's first object is reachable from it and\n *     every later one from the link word of the one before.  A thread-local\n *     head alone would not do, since Boehm does not scan thread-local storage\n *     on every platform; the thread-local variable only finds the block.  The\n *     block is never freed, so each thread that allocates keeps one, and the\n *     cells on its lists, for the life of the process.\n * Only the NORMAL kind takes this path.  A pointer-free object's link word is\n * never traced, so a PTRFREE list kept this way would lose all but its head.\n * The hit path copies libgc 8.2's free-list encoding, so other versions use\n * GC_malloc. */\n#if GC_VERSION_MAJOR == 8 && GC_VERSION_MINOR == 2\n\n/* The smallest request that does not fit an inline free list: n + 1 rounded up\n * to granules must stay below GC_TINY_FREELISTS. */\n#define MDK_ALLOC_INLINE_LIMIT ((GC_TINY_FREELISTS - 1) * GC_GRANULE_BYTES)\n\nstatic __thread void **mdk_alloc_freelists;\n\nstatic void **mdk_alloc_freelists_init(void) {\n  void **fl = GC_malloc_uncollectable(GC_TINY_FREELISTS * sizeof(void *));\n  mdk_alloc_freelists = fl;\n  return fl;\n}\n\n/* The whole of gc_inline.h's allocation: refill an empty list, or fall back to\n * GC_malloc.  Kept out of line so mdk_alloc's hit path saves no registers. */\nstatic __attribute__((noinline)) void *mdk_alloc_refill(long long n) {\n  size_t size = (size_t)n;\n  if (size >= MDK_ALLOC_INLINE_LIMIT) return GC_malloc(size);\n  size_t granules = (size + GC_GRANULE_BYTES) / GC_GRANULE_BYTES;\n  void **fl = mdk_alloc_freelists;\n  void *r;\n  if (fl == NULL) {\n    fl = mdk_alloc_freelists_init();\n    if (fl == NULL) return GC_malloc(size);\n  }\n  GC_FAST_MALLOC_GRANS(r, granules, fl, 0, GC_I_NORMAL, GC_malloc(size),\n                       *(void **)r = 0);\n  return r;\n}\n\n/* The hit branch of GC_FAST_MALLOC_GRANS for the NORMAL kind, step for step: a\n * list entry above GC_TINY_FREELISTS + 1 is an object, not a count or NULL.\n * noinline: inlined, this body makes small runtime helpers that box a result\n * (mdk_num_sub) too large for ThinLTO to inline into emitted code, and keeping\n * those helpers inlinable is worth more than a call here. */\n__attribute__((noinline)) void *mdk_alloc(long long n) {\n  size_t size = (size_t)n;\n  void **fl = mdk_alloc_freelists;\n  if (__builtin_expect(fl != NULL && size < MDK_ALLOC_INLINE_LIMIT, 1)) {\n    void **slot = fl + (size + GC_GRANULE_BYTES) / GC_GRANULE_BYTES;\n    void *r = *slot;\n    if (__builtin_expect((GC_word)r > GC_TINY_FREELISTS + 1, 1)) {\n      void *next = *(void **)r;\n      *slot = next;\n      *(void **)r = 0;\n      GC_PREFETCH_FOR_WRITE(next);\n      GC_end_stubborn_change(slot);\n      GC_reachable_here(next);\n      return r;\n    }\n  }\n  return mdk_alloc_refill(n);\n}\n\n#else\nvoid *mdk_alloc(long long n) { return GC_malloc((size_t)n); }\n#endif\n\n/* Allocate `n` bytes of POINTER-FREE memory (raw bytes / string cells).  Routes to\n * Boehm's GC_malloc_atomic: the block is never scanned for pointers during mark, so\n * the GC does not waste mark time walking string contents (the emitter produces an\n * enormous volume of transient string garbage).  Callers MUST fully initialise the\n * block before any read \u2014 GC_malloc_atomic does not zero \u2014 and the block MUST contain\n * no pointers the collector needs to follow.  String cells qualify: their header is\n * three integer words (tag, byte_len, cp_count) followed by raw UTF-8 bytes, all\n * written by mdk_str_lit; no field is a heap pointer.  The emitted IR declares this\n * with allockind(\"alloc,uninitialized\") and noalias: LLVM assumes the contents are\n * unspecified and that the call has no side effect beyond the allocation. */\nvoid *mdk_alloc_atomic(long long n) { return GC_malloc_atomic((size_t)n); }\n\n/* ---- generic arity-aware closure application (partial application / PAPs) ----\n *\n * A CLOSURE cell is `[ i64 arity | i64 code_ptr | captures... ]`: field 0 is the\n * closure's callable arity (the number of value args its lifted `@mdk_lamN` define\n * takes AFTER the leading `%clos` word), field 1 the code pointer.  The emitter\n * calls a closure INLINE (`code_ptr(cw, args...)`) only when it can prove the\n * supplied count equals the runtime arity; otherwise it routes through __mdk_apply.\n *\n * A PARTIAL APPLICATION (PAP) is `[ i64 -1 | i64 orig_cw | i64 n_supplied |\n * supplied_args... ]`: the -1 header sentinel (never equals a real supplied count\n * >= 1) forces every application of a PAP through __mdk_apply, which FLATTENS it \u2014\n * re-dispatching the original closure against (already-supplied ++ new) args.  So a\n * PAP is never called via the inline fast path and needs no per-arity trampoline. */\n#define MDK_MAX_ARITY 16\n\ntypedef long long mdk_i64;\n\nmdk_i64 __mdk_apply(mdk_i64 cw, mdk_i64 argc, const mdk_i64 *argv);\n\n/* call `code`(cw, argv[0..argc-1]) \u2014 argc statically-typed via a small switch. */\nstatic mdk_i64 mdk_call_exact(mdk_i64 code, mdk_i64 cw, mdk_i64 argc,\n                              const mdk_i64 *a) {\n  switch (argc) {\n    case 0:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64))code)(cw);\n    case 1:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0]);\n    case 2:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0],a[1]);\n    case 3:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0],a[1],a[2]);\n    case 4:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3]);\n    case 5:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3],a[4]);\n    case 6:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3],a[4],a[5]);\n    case 7:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3],a[4],a[5],a[6]);\n    case 8:  return ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)(cw,a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3],a[4],a[5],a[6],a[7]);\n    default:\n      /* arity > 8: saturate 8 at a time, then apply the surplus. */\n      {\n        mdk_i64 r = ((mdk_i64(*)(mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64,mdk_i64))code)\n                      (cw,a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3],a[4],a[5],a[6],a[7]);\n        return __mdk_apply(r, argc - 8, a + 8);\n      }\n  }\n}\n\n/* build a PAP capturing `cw` plus the `argc` args already supplied. */\nstatic mdk_i64 mdk_make_pap(mdk_i64 cw, mdk_i64 argc, const mdk_i64 *argv) {\n  mdk_i64 *cell = (mdk_i64 *)mdk_alloc((long long)(8 * (3 + argc)));\n  cell[0] = -1;         /* PAP sentinel header */\n  cell[1] = cw;         /* the original closure */\n  cell[2] = argc;       /* number of args captured so far */\n  for (mdk_i64 i = 0; i < argc; i++) cell[3 + i] = argv[i];\n  return (mdk_i64)cell;\n}\n\n/* apply the closure/PAP word `cw` to `argc` args (a pointer to `argc` i64 words).\n * The single entry point for any application the emitter could not resolve to an\n * exact-arity inline call. */\nmdk_i64 __mdk_apply(mdk_i64 cw, mdk_i64 argc, const mdk_i64 *argv) {\n  mdk_i64 *cell = (mdk_i64 *)cw;\n  if (cell[0] == -1) {\n    /* PAP: flatten \u2014 combine already-supplied args with the new ones and\n     * re-dispatch against the underlying closure. */\n    mdk_i64 orig = cell[1];\n    mdk_i64 nsup = cell[2];\n    mdk_i64 total = nsup + argc;\n    mdk_i64 stackbuf[2 * MDK_MAX_ARITY];\n    mdk_i64 *buf = stackbuf;\n    if (total > (mdk_i64)(2 * MDK_MAX_ARITY))\n      buf = (mdk_i64 *)mdk_alloc((long long)(8 * total));\n    for (mdk_i64 i = 0; i < nsup; i++) buf[i] = ((mdk_i64 *)cw)[3 + i];\n    for (mdk_i64 i = 0; i < argc; i++) buf[nsup + i] = argv[i];\n    return __mdk_apply(orig, total, buf);\n  }\n  {\n    mdk_i64 arity = cell[0];\n    mdk_i64 code = cell[1];\n    if (argc == arity) return mdk_call_exact(code, cw, argc, argv);\n    if (argc < arity) return mdk_make_pap(cw, argc, argv);\n    /* over-application: saturate `arity`, then apply the surplus to the result. */\n    {\n      mdk_i64 r = mdk_call_exact(code, cw, arity, argv);\n      return __mdk_apply(r, argc - arity, argv + arity);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n/* Forward-declared: defined below (near mdk_putstr) alongside the rest of the\n   \"run drops stdout on panic\" stash/flush machinery; mdk_oob is an abort path\n   that needs it but is emitted earlier in this file. */\nstatic void mdk_flush_run_stdout_on_abort(void);\n\nnoreturn void mdk_oob(void) {\n  mdk_flush_run_stdout_on_abort();\n  fprintf(stderr, \"runtime error [E-INDEX-OOB]: index out of bounds\\n\");\n  exit(1);\n}\n\n/* Out-of-range access raised by a container's own Index/IndexMut impl that already\n * knows what it wants to say (`indexError : String -> a`), as opposed to mdk_oob_at\n * below, which is handed a bare index and does the wording here.  A container keyed\n * by something other than an Int -- a map, a set -- has no number to interpolate, so\n * the message has to travel.\n *\n * `w` is a tagged pointer to a Medaka string cell, the same rep mdk_panic reads: byte\n * length in word 1, bytes at +24.  Unlike mdk_panic there is no 0x01-sentinel branch,\n * because no caller here hands over a pre-formatted diagnostic -- every one passes\n * plain prose, so the coded banner is unconditional. */\nnoreturn void mdk_oob_msg(long long w) {\n  mdk_flush_run_stdout_on_abort();\n  const char *cell = (const char *)w;\n  long long byte_len = ((const long long *)cell)[1];\n  fputs(\"runtime error [E-INDEX-OOB]: \", stderr);\n  fwrite(cell + 24, 1, (size_t)byte_len, stderr);\n  fputc('\\n', stderr);\n  exit(1);\n}\n\n/* Out-of-range `arr[i]` / `arr[i] := v` raised by a container's OWN Index/IndexMut\n * impl, carrying the offending index (#1787).  `idx` is a RAW (already >>1-untagged)\n * i64, matching mdk_slice_oob's convention.\n *\n * Why this exists rather than letting the impl interpolate its own message and pass\n * it to mdk_oob: mdk_oob takes no argument, so the message the impl built was\n * evaluated and DISCARDED on native -- `run` printed \"index 7 out of bounds\" while a\n * built binary printed \"index out of bounds\" for the same program.  The dead\n * interpolation was not free: it cost ~10 points of LLVM inline cost, which put\n * `index`/`setIndex` at 235 against a threshold of 225 and stopped them being inlined\n * into hot loops, making `arr[i] := v` ~15% slower than the `Array.set` function it\n * desugars to.  Formatting here fixes both: the engines agree, and the impl's cold\n * branch is one call. */\nnoreturn void mdk_oob_at(long long idx) {\n  mdk_flush_run_stdout_on_abort();\n  fprintf(stderr, \"runtime error [E-INDEX-OOB]: index %lld out of bounds\\n\", idx);\n  exit(1);\n}\n\n/* Out-of-range `arr.[lo..hi]` / `arr.[lo..=hi]` (#550).  The emitted slice used to\n * allocate `end - lo` slots and copy `a[lo + i]` with NO bounds check, so an\n * over-range slice READ OFF THE END OF THE HEAP and surfaced whatever it found \u2014\n * including live pointers \u2014 as ordinary Ints, at exit 0.  `run` raised E-SLICE-OOB\n * all along (sliceArray, compiler/eval/eval.mdk); only the native path was unchecked.\n *\n * `lo`/`hi_incl` are RAW (already >>1-untagged) i64s, and `hi_incl` is the INCLUSIVE\n * upper bound (end - 1) so the text is byte-identical to the interpreter's\n * `slice [\\{lo}..\\{hiX - 1}] out of bounds`.  Unlike mdk_oob (whose message carries no\n * number, so it needs no args) exact parity with `run` is cheap here: this is an abort\n * path, so the two extra argument words cost nothing on the hot path. */\nnoreturn void mdk_slice_oob(long long lo, long long hi_incl) {\n  mdk_flush_run_stdout_on_abort();\n  fprintf(stderr, \"runtime error [E-SLICE-OOB]: slice [%lld..%lld] out of bounds\\n\",\n          lo, hi_incl);\n  exit(1);\n}\n\n/* #561 PR-A: a top-level nullary value global that refers to itself during its own\n * initialization (a non-productive cyclic value, e.g. `x = x + 1`, or a mutual\n * `a = b; b = a`).  The native backend emits such globals LAZILY \u2014 forced on first\n * use, with a per-global state flag (@mdk_gs_<name>) black-holed to state 1 while the\n * body runs \u2014 and re-entering a still-forcing cell calls this, matching the reference\n * engine (eval)'s forceMemo/blackholeCell E-CYCLIC-VALUE.  `name` is a static C string\n * naming the offending binding.  Flushes buffered stdout on the abort path exactly as\n * mdk_oob/mdk_slice_oob do (the \"run drops stdout on panic\" machinery). */\nnoreturn void mdk_cyclic_value(const char* name) {\n  mdk_flush_run_stdout_on_abort();\n  fprintf(stderr,\n          \"runtime error [E-CYCLIC-VALUE]: %s refers to itself during initialization (non-productive cyclic value)\\n\",\n          name);\n  exit(1);\n}\n\n/* Print an Int.  Matches the tree-walker oracle: Eval.pp_value (VInt n) =\n * string_of_int n, then eval_probe adds a trailing newline. */\nvoid mdk_print_int(long long v) { printf(\"%lld\\n\", v); }\n\n/* Print a Bool for the VALUE-MAIN auto-print (emitPrint LTBool -> the sole caller;\n * llvm_emit.mdk's `if mainIsUnit e mty then () else emitPrint e mv mty`).\n *\n * Renders the CONSTRUCTOR names `True`/`False` \u2014 Medaka's own `impl Display Bool`\n * (stdlib/core.mdk: `display True = \"True\"`).  That is the contract a SHIPPING\n * binary produces: `medaka build` runs the composite-main auto-print wrap\n * (compiler/driver/main_autoprint.mdk), which rewrites `main = <e>` into\n * `main = println <e>`, so a Bool value-main renders through `display`.  The WasmGC\n * backend's peer ($mdk_print_bool in compiler/backend/wasm_preamble.mdk) already\n * writes \"True\"/\"False\", with a comment saying it MUST agree with native's\n * println/display \u2014 this function was the last holdout.\n *\n * It previously printed OCaml's `string_of_bool` (\"true\"/\"false\") to match the\n * OCaml oracle's Eval.pp_value.  That oracle was REMOVED 2026-06-26, so the\n * lowercase rendering survived only in the PRELUDE-FREE emit probes\n * (test/bin/llvm_emit_main), where no `println` is in scope and the wrap cannot\n * fire.  That is why test/diff_compiler_llvm.sh was grading a rendering no\n * `medaka build` binary can ever emit. */\nvoid mdk_print_bool(long long v) { printf(v ? \"True\\n\" : \"False\\n\"); }\n\n/* Render the canonical Medaka float lexeme into `out` (needs >= 32 bytes).\n *\n * DECIDED 2026-06-15 / REVISED 2026-07-15 (issue #57): SHORTEST-ROUND-TRIP.  The\n * lexeme is the fewest significant digits that `strtod` reads back to the\n * bit-identical double \u2014 so `debug (0.1 + 0.2)` renders \"0.30000000000000004\",\n * not the old \"%.12g\" truncation \"0.3\".  Digits come from `%.*e` at the smallest\n * precision whose round-trip is bit-exact (compared as uint64 bit patterns, not\n * `double ==`, so a NaN can never spuriously match).\n *\n * The EXPONENT THRESHOLD is unchanged from the historical \"%.12g\" rule\n * (scientific iff decimal exponent < -4 or >= 12), so whole/round values still\n * print \"N.0\" (100.0, not \"1e+02\") and only values that genuinely need >12 sig\n * digits move.  Scientific form is lowercase 'e' + sign + 2-digit-padded exponent\n * (e.g. \"1e-07\", \"1e+20\"), which the post-#51 lexer reads back.  The \".0\" append\n * rule tags a bare-integer lexeme (no '.'/'e').  inf/nan pass through untouched\n * (\"inf\"/\"-inf\"/\"nan\"), never the loop.  This helper is the SINGLE source of truth\n * shared by mdk_print_float (bare-Float auto-print) and mdk_float_to_string (the\n * floatToString extern) \u2014 they MUST stay byte-identical, and both mirror the JS\n * host copies in test/wasm/run.js and playground/worker.js. */\nstatic void mdk_float_lexeme(double d, char *out) {\n  if (isnan(d)) { strcpy(out, \"nan\"); return; }\n  if (isinf(d)) { strcpy(out, d < 0 ? \"-inf\" : \"inf\"); return; }\n  if (d == 0.0) { strcpy(out, (1.0 / d < 0) ? \"-0.0\" : \"0.0\"); return; }\n\n  /* shortest significant-digit count: %.*e with precision p-1 == p sig digits. */\n  char sci[64];\n  int p;\n  for (p = 1; p <= 17; p++) {\n    snprintf(sci, sizeof sci, \"%.*e\", p - 1, d);\n    double rt = strtod(sci, NULL);\n    uint64_t a, b;\n    memcpy(&a, &rt, 8);\n    memcpy(&b, &d, 8);\n    if (a == b) break;\n  }\n  if (p > 17) snprintf(sci, sizeof sci, \"%.*e\", 16, d);\n\n  /* parse sci = [-]d[.ddd]e(+|-)XX into sign, digit string, decimal exponent. */\n  const char *s = sci;\n  int neg = 0;\n  if (*s == '-') { neg = 1; s++; }\n  char digits[40];\n  int nd = 0;\n  digits[nd++] = *s++;                 /* leading significant digit */\n  if (*s == '.') { s++; while (*s != 'e' && *s != 'E') digits[nd++] = *s++; }\n  int exp = atoi(s + 1);               /* s points at 'e' */\n  digits[nd] = '\\0';\n  while (nd > 1 && digits[nd - 1] == '0') digits[--nd] = '\\0';  /* trim (defensive) */\n\n  char body[80];\n  if (exp < -4 || exp >= 12) {\n    char mant[48];\n    if (nd == 1) { mant[0] = digits[0]; mant[1] = '\\0'; }\n    else { mant[0] = digits[0]; mant[1] = '.'; strcpy(mant + 2, digits + 1); }\n    snprintf(body, sizeof body, \"%se%c%02d\", mant, exp < 0 ? '-' : '+',\n             exp < 0 ? -exp : exp);\n  } else {\n    int pp = exp + 1;                  /* digits before the decimal point */\n    if (pp <= 0) {\n      char z[24];\n      int i;\n      for (i = 0; i < -pp; i++) z[i] = '0';\n      z[i] = '\\0';\n      snprintf(body, sizeof body, \"0.%s%s\", z, digits);\n    } else if (pp >= nd) {\n      char z[24];\n      int i;\n      for (i = 0; i < pp - nd; i++) z[i] = '0';\n      z[i] = '\\0';\n      snprintf(body, sizeof body, \"%s%s\", digits, z);\n    } else {\n      char head[40];\n      memcpy(head, digits, (size_t)pp);\n      head[pp] = '\\0';\n      snprintf(body, sizeof body, \"%s.%s\", head, digits + pp);\n    }\n  }\n\n  char full[96];\n  if (neg) snprintf(full, sizeof full, \"-%s\", body);\n  else     snprintf(full, sizeof full, \"%s\", body);\n  if (!strpbrk(full, \".eEni\")) strcat(full, \".0\");  /* bare-int lexeme -> N.0 */\n  strcpy(out, full);\n}\n\n/* Print a bare Float (the auto-print sink) via the shared canonical lexeme. */\nvoid mdk_print_float(double d) {\n  char buf[96];\n  mdk_float_lexeme(d, buf);\n  printf(\"%s\\n\", buf);\n}\n\n/* \u2500\u2500 Strings (native extern catalog, slice 1) \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n * STRING REPRESENTATION \u2014 LOCKED 2026-06-07 (RUNTIME-DESIGN.md \u00a74 / \u00a77 decision\n * 2): UTF-8 bytes + a CACHED codepoint count, boxed as one GC cell:\n *\n *   offset  0:  i64 header     layout id (MDK_STR_TAG; not yet tag-tested \u2014 no\n *                              String match heads in this slice)\n *   offset  8:  i64 byte_len   number of UTF-8 bytes (raw / untagged)\n *   offset 16:  i64 cp_count   cached codepoint count  ->  stringLength is O(1)\n *   offset 24:  byte_len bytes of UTF-8, then a NUL (for cheap C interop)\n *\n * Caching cp_count is the choice \u00a74 calls for (Medaka is codepoint-aware): it\n * makes `stringLength` INTRINSIC (a header read) rather than an O(n) scan \u2014 see\n * the \u00a75 (rep)-row reconciliation in RUNTIME-DESIGN.md.  The cell rides the same\n * one-word-header boxed-pointer discipline (\u00a78.1 / \u00a78.4) as every other heap\n * value, so it is GC-managed for free under Boehm: the value word is an aligned\n * pointer (low bit 0) Boehm tracks, and the inline bytes are scanned harmlessly.\n *\n * Per \u00a72a, every extern that RETURNS a Medaka String allocates it here, through\n * mdk_alloc, with this exact layout \u2014 it never hands back a\n * native-owned buffer.  mdk_int_to_string is the first such extern. */\n#define MDK_STR_TAG 1\n\n/* BYTEBLOCK REPRESENTATION \u2014 the packed byte buffer behind the `ByteBlock`\n * builtin (stdlib/runtime.mdk, \"Byte blocks\"), boxed as one GC cell:\n *\n *   offset  0:  i64 header     MDK_BYTEBLOCK_TAG\n *   offset  8:  i64 count      number of bytes (raw / untagged)\n *   offset 16:  count bytes, padded up to a whole word\n *\n * The header sits at offset 0, unlike the array cell, whose word 0 is its raw\n * element count -- so a length-1 array is indistinguishable from a String cell\n * and a byte block must not be given that shape.  The value is a composite in\n * the reserved type-id range (slot 4; see the MDK_TAG block below and\n * `reservedTag` in compiler/backend/llvm_emit.mdk), which no user constructor\n * tag and no other cell header can reach.  The _Static_assert beside MDK_TAG\n * pins this spelling to that formula.\n *\n * The payload holds no pointers and the two header words are integers, so the\n * cell is allocated pointer-free through mdk_alloc_atomic, exactly as a String\n * cell is; mdk_alloc_atomic does not zero, so mdk_byteblock_alloc memsets. */\n#define MDK_BYTEBLOCK_TAG ((65536LL + 4LL) * 4294967296LL)\n\n/* U64 REPRESENTATION \u2014 the boxed 64-bit unsigned integer behind the `U64`\n * builtin (docs/design/INTEGER-TYPES-DESIGN.md section 6.2), Float's cell shape:\n *\n *   offset  0:  i64 header     MDK_U64_TAG\n *   offset  8:  u64 payload    the value, all 64 bits\n *\n * The header is reserved type-id 5 (`u64CellTag` in\n * compiler/backend/llvm_emit.mdk), pinned to MDK_TAG(5, 0) beside the byte\n * block's assertion.  The cell holds no pointers, so it is allocated through\n * mdk_alloc_atomic; a literal is a private constant cell the emitter lays out\n * the same way, so nothing may write through a U64 word.  The type-lost\n * discriminators below (mdk_value_eq, mdk_value_cmp_raw, mdk_value_lt/le/gt/ge,\n * mdk_num_*, mdk_print_num) order and compute on the unsigned payload. */\n#define MDK_U64_TAG ((65536LL + 5LL) * 4294967296LL)\n\nstatic int mdk_is_u64(long long w) {\n  return ((w & 1) == 0) && ((const long long *)w)[0] == MDK_U64_TAG;\n}\n\nstatic unsigned long long mdk_u64_payload(long long w) {\n  return ((const unsigned long long *)w)[1];\n}\n\nstatic long long mdk_box_u64(unsigned long long x) {\n  long long *c = (long long *)mdk_alloc_atomic(16);\n  c[0] = MDK_U64_TAG;\n  ((unsigned long long *)c)[1] = x;\n  return (long long)c;\n}\n\n/* The auto-print sink for a `U64` result: the decimal value, as the\n * interpreter's `ppValue (VU64 \u2026)` renders it. */\nvoid mdk_print_u64(long long w) { printf(\"%llu\\n\", mdk_u64_payload(w)); }\n\n/* I64 REPRESENTATION \u2014 the boxed 64-bit signed integer behind the `I64` builtin:\n * U64's cell shape and payload, the 64 bits read in two's complement, under a\n * header of its own (reserved type-id 6, `i64CellTag` in\n * compiler/backend/llvm_emit.mdk, pinned to MDK_TAG(6, 0) below).  The distinct\n * header is what lets the type-lost discriminators order, divide and print an\n * I64 signed where a U64 is unsigned. */\n#define MDK_I64_TAG ((65536LL + 6LL) * 4294967296LL)\n\nstatic int mdk_is_i64(long long w) {\n  return ((w & 1) == 0) && ((const long long *)w)[0] == MDK_I64_TAG;\n}\n\nstatic long long mdk_i64_payload(long long w) {\n  return ((const long long *)w)[1];\n}\n\nstatic long long mdk_box_i64(long long x) {\n  long long *c = (long long *)mdk_alloc_atomic(16);\n  c[0] = MDK_I64_TAG;\n  c[1] = x;\n  return (long long)c;\n}\n\n/* `/` and `%` at I64: truncating, as C's, with `minBound / -1` wrapping to\n * minBound and `minBound % -1` giving 0 (C's own quotient there is undefined). */\nstatic long long mdk_i64_div(long long a, long long b) {\n  return b == -1 ? (long long)(0ULL - (unsigned long long)a) : a / b;\n}\n\nstatic long long mdk_i64_mod(long long a, long long b) {\n  return b == -1 ? 0 : a % b;\n}\n\n/* The auto-print sink for an `I64` result: the signed decimal value. */\nvoid mdk_print_i64(long long w) { printf(\"%lld\\n\", mdk_i64_payload(w)); }\n\n/* Byte-block content discriminators, used by mdk_value_eq / mdk_value_cmp_raw /\n * mdk_append below; defined with the rest of the byte-block family, beside the\n * array leaf helpers it mirrors. */\nstatic int mdk_is_byteblock(long long w);\nstatic long long mdk_byteblock_cmp_bytes(long long a, long long b);\nnoreturn static void mdk_byteblock_append_unsupported(void);\n\n/* mdk_append's fail-closed arm: a left operand that is neither String, byte block,\n * Nil nor Cons must not be walked as a Cons chain.  Both read the reserved ADT tags\n * MDK_TAG_CONS/MDK_TAG_NIL, so they are defined down beside those. */\nstatic int mdk_is_list_word(long long w);\nnoreturn static void mdk_append_unsupported(void);\n\n/* Count UTF-8 codepoints in the first `n` bytes of `p`: every byte that is not a\n * 0b10xxxxxx continuation byte starts a new codepoint.  Exact only on\n * well-formed UTF-8, which every String cell holds: bytes from outside the\n * program reach a cell only through mdk_str_lossy or a validating producer. */\nstatic long long mdk_utf8_cp_count(const char *p, long long n) {\n  long long c = 0;\n  for (long long i = 0; i < n; i++)\n    if (((unsigned char)p[i] & 0xC0) != 0x80) c++;\n  return c;\n}\n\n/* The byte length (1..4) of the well-formed UTF-8 sequence starting at p[i],\n * or the negated length of its maximal ill-formed subpart: the bytes accepted\n * before the sequence failed, or 1 when it failed on its lead.  `C0`/`C1` and\n * `F5` upwards are not leads; an `E0`/`F0` lead bounds its second byte below\n * (overlong), `ED` above (surrogate) and `F4` above (past U+10FFFF).  The same\n * rule, subpart for subpart, as `utf8StepAt` in stdlib/bytes.mdk and\n * `$mdk_utf8_step` in compiler/backend/wasm_preamble.mdk. */\nstatic int mdk_utf8_step(const unsigned char *p, size_t i, size_t n) {\n  unsigned char b0 = p[i];\n  if (b0 <= 0x7F) return 1;\n  if (b0 >= 0xC2 && b0 <= 0xDF)\n    return (i + 1 < n && (p[i + 1] & 0xC0) == 0x80) ? 2 : -1;\n  if (b0 >= 0xE0 && b0 <= 0xF4) {\n    int wide = b0 >= 0xF0;\n    unsigned char lo = (b0 == 0xE0) ? 0xA0 : (b0 == 0xF0) ? 0x90 : 0x80;\n    unsigned char hi = (b0 == 0xED) ? 0x9F : (b0 == 0xF4) ? 0x8F : 0xBF;\n    if (i + 1 >= n || p[i + 1] < lo || p[i + 1] > hi) return -1;\n    if (i + 2 >= n || (p[i + 2] & 0xC0) != 0x80) return -2;\n    if (!wide) return 3;\n    if (i + 3 >= n || (p[i + 3] & 0xC0) != 0x80) return -3;\n    return 4;\n  }\n  return -1;\n}\n\n/* The codepoint count of p[0..n) when it is well-formed UTF-8, else -1.  Eight\n * ASCII bytes at a time until the first non-ASCII byte, so the common input\n * costs about one load and one test per word. */\nstatic long long mdk_utf8_valid_count(const char *s, size_t n) {\n  const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s;\n  size_t i = 0;\n  long long c = 0;\n  while (i < n) {\n    if (i + 8 <= n) {\n      uint64_t w;\n      memcpy(&w, p + i, 8);\n      if ((w & 0x8080808080808080ULL) == 0) { i += 8; c += 8; continue; }\n    }\n    if (p[i] < 0x80) { i++; c++; continue; }\n    int st = mdk_utf8_step(p, i, n);\n    if (st < 0) return -1;\n    i += (size_t)st;\n    c++;\n  }\n  return c;\n}\n\n/* Validate one complete byte range as canonical UTF-8 encoding Unicode scalar\n * values: the trust-boundary check for bytes supplied by foreign C code. */\nstatic int mdk_utf8_is_valid(const char *p, size_t n) {\n  return mdk_utf8_valid_count(p, n) >= 0;\n}\n\n/* A String cell holding `byte_len` bytes whose codepoint count the caller\n * already knows.  The bytes must be well-formed UTF-8. */\nstatic long long mdk_str_cell(const char *bytes, long long byte_len,\n                              long long cp_count) {\n  char *cell = (char *)mdk_alloc_atomic(24 + byte_len + 1);\n  ((long long *)cell)[0] = MDK_STR_TAG;\n  ((long long *)cell)[1] = byte_len;\n  ((long long *)cell)[2] = cp_count;\n  memcpy(cell + 24, bytes, (size_t)byte_len);\n  cell[24 + byte_len] = '\\0';\n  return (long long)cell;\n}\n\n/* Build a boxed String cell from `byte_len` bytes of well-formed UTF-8 that the\n * runtime or the program itself produced (a literal, a rendered number, a\n * slice of an existing String); return the value word (cell pointer as i64,\n * low bit 0).  Bytes from outside the program go through mdk_str_lossy. */\nlong long mdk_str_lit(const char *bytes, long long byte_len) {\n  return mdk_str_cell(bytes, byte_len, mdk_utf8_cp_count(bytes, byte_len));\n}\n\n/* A String cell from bytes of unknown provenance: verbatim when they are\n * well-formed UTF-8, otherwise with one U+FFFD (`EF BF BD`) substituted for\n * each maximal ill-formed subpart, exactly as `bytes.decodeUtf8Lossy` does.\n * Every producer that turns outside bytes into a String routes through here or\n * validates them itself. */\nstatic long long mdk_str_lossy(const char *bytes, long long byte_len) {\n  long long valid = mdk_utf8_valid_count(bytes, (size_t)byte_len);\n  if (valid >= 0) return mdk_str_cell(bytes, byte_len, valid);\n  const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)bytes;\n  size_t n = (size_t)byte_len, out = 0;\n  for (size_t i = 0; i < n;) {\n    int st = mdk_utf8_step(p, i, n);\n    if (st > 0) { out += (size_t)st; i += (size_t)st; }\n    else { out += 3; i += (size_t)-st; }\n  }\n  char *cell = (char *)mdk_alloc_atomic(24 + out + 1);\n  char *dst = cell + 24;\n  size_t j = 0;\n  long long cps = 0;\n  for (size_t i = 0; i < n; cps++) {\n    int st = mdk_utf8_step(p, i, n);\n    if (st > 0) {\n      memcpy(dst + j, p + i, (size_t)st);\n      j += (size_t)st; i += (size_t)st;\n    } else {\n      dst[j] = (char)0xEF; dst[j + 1] = (char)0xBF; dst[j + 2] = (char)0xBD;\n      j += 3; i += (size_t)-st;\n    }\n  }\n  ((long long *)cell)[0] = MDK_STR_TAG;\n  ((long long *)cell)[1] = (long long)out;\n  ((long long *)cell)[2] = cps;\n  dst[out] = '\\0';\n  return (long long)cell;\n}\n\n/* String equality on two boxed String cells.  Returns a TAGGED Medaka Bool word\n * (3 = True, 1 = False, matching the emitter's `if b then \"3\" else \"1\"` rep), so\n * the literal-switch emitter can `icmp eq i64 r, 3` to branch.  Two strings are\n * equal iff equal byte_len and byte-identical payload (codepoint count is a cache\n * of byte content, so byte_len + memcmp is sufficient and exact). */\nlong long mdk_string_eq(long long a, long long b) {\n  const char *ca = (const char *)a;\n  const char *cb = (const char *)b;\n  long long la = ((const long long *)ca)[1];\n  long long lb = ((const long long *)cb)[1];\n  if (la != lb) return 1;\n  if (memcmp(ca + 24, cb + 24, (size_t)la) != 0) return 1;\n  return 3;\n}\n\n/* Polymorphic `==`/`!=` for operands whose static LTy the emitter could not\n * recover (both default to LTInt \u2014 e.g. a `feq a b = a == b` over inferred-Float\n * params, or two String-typed params whose only use is `n == name`).\n * Discriminates at run time on the low bit / header tag, the EXACT peer of\n * mdk_value_cmp_raw's Ord discriminator (they MUST stay in lockstep):\n *   - boxed String cell (even pointer, header == MDK_STR_TAG) -> byte compare;\n *   - boxed Float cell  (even pointer, header == 2)           -> double compare\n *     (issue #181: without this arm two independently-boxed floats compared as\n *     value words \u2014 i.e. by POINTER \u2014 so `feq 0.5 0.5` was False in native);\n *   - otherwise (tagged immediates \u2014 Int/Bool/Char, nullary-ctor words) compares\n *     by value word. }\nvoid mdk_flushstdout(long long w) {\n  (void)w;\n  fflush(stdout);\n  mdk_build_stdout_flushed();\n}\nvoid mdk_print_unit(void)       { printf(\"()\\n\"); }\n\n/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * \"run drops stdout on panic\" fix.  `medaka run`'s tree-walking interpreter\n * buffers a program's stdout in an in-language Ref<String> (eval.mdk's\n * outputRef) and only writes it to real stdout via ONE final `putStr` call\n * after `main` returns NORMALLY (medaka_cli.mdk's `runProgramOutput`).\n * Medaka panics are NOT catchable (no exception handling, no unwind), so a\n * panicking program's buffered stdout used to be silently discarded \u2014 the\n * printed trace before the crash never reached the terminal, which made the\n * standard \"does this ill-typed program actually EXECUTE\" probe (`println`\n * a sentinel, then check whether it appears) blind: both `run`'s stdout AND\n * its exit code look identical whether the program ran or not.\n *\n * mdk_stash_run_stdout lets eval.mdk register the buffer's raw bytes (a\n * pointer + length into an already-allocated, GC-owned, IMMUTABLE string\n * cell -- storing the pointer performs no allocation and no observable\n * effect) after every print.  mdk_enable_run_stdout_flush is called exactly\n * once, only by the real `medaka run` CLI driver (evalModulesOutputRun /\n * evalModulesOutputAsync) -- never by the pure differential-oracle eval\n * probes, which share this exact source but never call it, so their\n * captured output (many goldens pin an EMPTY capture for a deliberately\n * panicking fixture) is unaffected. i < n; i++) buf[off++] = enc[i];\n  buf[off++] = '\\'';\n  return mdk_str_lit(buf, off);\n}\n\n/* \u2500\u2500 perf / instrumentation externs \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n * wallTimeSec : Unit -> <IO> Float   \u2014 wall-clock seconds (gettimeofday).\n * allocBytes  : Unit -> <IO> Float   \u2014 total GC-heap bytes allocated since start.\n * Both return a boxed Float word (mdk_box_float), identical ABI to randomFloat. */\n\nlong long mdk_wall_time_sec(long long u) { (void)u;\n  struct timeval tv;\n  gettimeofday(&tv, NULL);\n  return mdk_box_float((double)tv.tv_sec + (double)tv.tv_usec * 1e-6);\n}\n\nlong long mdk_alloc_bytes(long long u) { (void)u;\n  return mdk_box_float((double)GC_get_total_bytes());\n}\n\n/* monotonicSec : Unit -> <Clock> Float \u2014 monotonic clock seconds (immune to\n * wall-clock adjustment).  clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) is POSIX and available\n * on macOS. Other executables\n * retain POSIX's default SIGTERM disposition unless they call this extern. */\nstatic volatile sig_atomic_t mdk_pds_term_seen = 0;\nstatic int mdk_pds_term_write_fd = -1;\nstatic int mdk_pds_term_read_fd = -1;\n\nstatic void mdk_pds_term_handler(int signum) {\n  (void)signum;\n  int saved = errno;\n  mdk_pds_term_seen = 1;\n  unsigned char byte = 1;\n  if (mdk_pds_term_write_fd >= 0)\n    (void)write(mdk_pds_term_write_fd, &byte, 1);\n  errno = saved;\n}\n\n/* pdsSignalStart : Unit -> Result String Int; called once after binding.\n * Both ends are nonblocking and close-on-exec; a failed setup leaves the\n * process's prior SIGTERM disposition untouched. */\nlong long mdk_pds_signal_start(long long unit) {\n  (void)unit;\n  if (mdk_pds_term_read_fd >= 0)\n    return mdk_err(mdk_str_cstr(\"pdsSignalStart: already installed\"));\n  int ends[2];\n  if (pipe(ends) != 0) return mdk_err(mdk_str_cstr(strerror(errno)));\n  for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {\n    int flags = fcntl(ends[i], F_GETFL, 0);\n    int fdflags = fcntl(ends[i], F_GETFD, 0);\n    if (flags < 0 || fdflags < 0 ||\n        fcntl(ends[i], F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK) != 0 ||\n        fcntl(ends[i], F_SETFD, fdflags | FD_CLOEXEC) != 0) {\n      int err = errno;\n      close(ends[0]); close(ends[1]);\n      return mdk_err(mdk_str_cstr(strerror(err)));\n    }\n  }\n  struct sigaction action = {0};\n  action.sa_handler = mdk_pds_term_handler;\n  sigemptyset(&action.sa_mask);\n  mdk_pds_term_seen = 0;\n  mdk_pds_term_write_fd = ends[1];\n  if (sigaction(SIGTERM, &action, NULL) != 0) {\n    int err = errno;\n    mdk_pds_term_write_fd = -1;\n    close(ends[0]); close(ends[1]);\n    return mdk_err(mdk_str_cstr(strerror(err)));\n  }\n  mdk_pds_term_read_fd = ends[0];\n  return mdk_ok(MDK_NET_TAG(ends[0]));\n}\n\n/* pdsSignalRequested : Unit -> Bool. None = would-block; Some n = bytes\n * written from `offset` (may be short, never more than the chunk). */\nlong long mdk_net_try_send_from(long long fd_tagged, long long arr, long long off_tagged) {\n  const long long *a = (const long long *)arr;\n  long long len = a[0];\n  long long off = off_tagged >> 1;\n  if (off < 0) off = 0;\n  if (off > len) off = len;\n  long long n = len - off;\n  if (n > MDK_SEND_CHUNK) n = MDK_SEND_CHUNK;\n  unsigned char *buf = (unsigned char *)mdk_alloc(n ? n : 1);\n  for (long long i = 0; i < n; i++) buf[i] = (unsigned char)((a[off + i + 1] >> 1) & 0xFF);\n  int flags = 0;\n#ifdef MSG_NOSIGNAL\n  flags = MSG_NOSIGNAL;\n#endif\n  ssize_t w = send(MDK_NET_UNTAG(fd_tagged), buf, (size_t)n, flags);\n  if (w < 0) {\n    if (mdk_net_would_block(errno)) return mdk_ok(mdk_none());\n    return mdk_err(mdk_str_cstr(strerror(errno)));\n  }\n  return mdk_ok(mdk_some(MDK_NET_TAG((long long)w)));\n}\n\n/* The window [start, end) of a ByteBlock that netSendBytesFrom and\n * netTrySendBytesFrom send.  Unlike the clamping Array Int senders above, a\n * window outside the block is refused: returns 0 and sets *err to the Err\n * value; otherwise returns 1 and sets *n to the byte count, capped at\n * MDK_SEND_CHUNK.  send(2) reads the block's own payload, so nothing is\n * copied. */\nstatic int mdk_net_send_window(const char *who, long long bb, long long start,\n                               long long end, long long *n, long long *err) {\n  long long len = mdk_byteblock_count(bb);\n  if (start < 0 || end < start || end > len) {\n    char msg[160];\n    snprintf(msg, sizeof msg,\n             \"%s: window [%lld, %lld) is outside a block of %lld bytes\",\n             who, start, end, len);\n    *err = mdk_err(mdk_str_cstr(msg));\n    return 0;\n  }\n  *n = end - start;\n  if (*n > MDK_SEND_CHUNK) *n = MDK_SEND_CHUNK;\n  return 1;\n}\n\n/* netSendBytesFrom : fd -> ByteBlock -> start -> end -> Result String Int. */\nlong long mdk_net_send_bytes_from(long long fd_tagged, long long bb,\n                                  long long start_tagged, long long end_tagged) {\n  long long start = start_tagged >> 1, n = 0, err = 0;\n  if (!mdk_net_send_window(\"netSendBytesFrom\", bb, start, end_tagged >> 1, &n, &err))\n    return err;\n  int flags = 0;\n#ifdef MSG_NOSIGNAL\n  flags = MSG_NOSIGNAL;\n#endif\n  ssize_t w = send(MDK_NET_UNTAG(fd_tagged), mdk_byteblock_bytes(bb) + start,\n                   (size_t)n, flags);\n  if (w < 0) return mdk_err(mdk_str_cstr(strerror(errno)));\n  return mdk_ok(MDK_NET_TAG((long long)w));\n}\n\n/* netTrySendBytesFrom : fd -> ByteBlock -> start -> end\n *   -> Result String (Option Int).
